topic: Analysing the Strategic Position of a Business
subject: business-studies

items.q: When might an autocratic leadership style be appropriate?
items.correct: In crises requiring quick decisions, when workers are inexperienced, or in highly hierarchical contexts — though it can damage morale long-term.
items.misconception: Autocratic leadership is always wrong and democratic leadership is always right.
items.random_wrong: Autocratic leaders are dictators who break the law.
items.why: Students moralise leadership styles. The business studies view is contingency-based — each style has appropriate contexts. Democratic is not universally best; autocracy works in emergencies.

items.q: Porter's three generic strategies are cost leadership, differentiation and:
items.why: The answer examiners want is: Focus. “Diversification” is the distractor this question was built around — if it tempted you, that's the exact gap to close.

items.q: The 'Blue Ocean' concept was proposed by:
items.why: The answer examiners want is: Kim and Mauborgne. “Porter” is the distractor this question was built around — if it tempted you, that's the exact gap to close.

items.q: How many generic strategies did Porter identify?
items.why: Exact answer: 3 strategies. Estimation gets you near it; only the anchored number survives the exam hall.
